name: LoL Catalog Nexus (Tauri + Vite)
description: Desktop League of Legends cosmetics catalog: offline-first Tauri app, optional live client integration, schema-versioned local data, and bundled asset prefetch.
longDescription: A desktop catalog for champions, skins, and chromas that boots quickly from a local database and bundled assets. Rust owns domain logic, storage, and optional read-only integration with the game client; a Vite and TypeScript UI provides search, sync status, and 3D skin preview. Public game data is prefetched at build time to avoid runtime CDN dependency. Schema versioning keeps UI and storage aligned across upgrades. Automated tests cover local database and adapter behaviour.
features: Offline-first catalog with optional live client read-only mode
Schema-versioned local database and generated TypeScript types
Build-time asset prefetch for fast, predictable startup
3D skin preview and modular app shell
Explicit desktop API boundary instead of direct shell access
Unit tests for storage and client adapter logic
highlights: Fast offline experience with optional live enrichment
Single schema contract across Rust storage and TypeScript UI
Build pipeline that validates and bundles public game metadata
challenges: Large catalogs need disciplined caching without stale or oversized bundles.
solutions: Versioned schema, scripted prefetch, and separation between bundled data and optional live calls.
security: Live client integration is local-only and read-only
No player credentials stored in the offline catalog
